title: Blend-Out of Corrosion Damage on the Fwd Lower Shell Skin Adjacent to the Lap Joint
abstract: Removal of surface and intergranular corrosion from the forward lower shell skin next to the longitudinal lap joint by controlled blending, with the depth limits and the protection restoration that follow.

sections.purpose: This task removes corrosion from the forward lower shell skin next to the longitudinal lap joint by controlled blending, and restores the surface protection, provided the remaining thickness stays inside the published limit.
sections.job_setup_note: Establish the nominal skin thickness from the structural repair data before you start, because the blend limit is a percentage of it. Ultrasonic thickness measurement is required before and after blending and the readings must be recorded on the blend map. Corrosion that reaches a fastener hole or crosses the joint line is outside the scope of this task.
sections.procedure: 1. Get access from the forward and aft cargo compartments and remove the lining local to the damage. 2. Clean the area and define the extent of the corrosion with the approved developer. 3. Measure and record the skin thickness at nine points on a 25 millimetre grid over the damage. 4. Blend the corrosion out with a rotary file and progressively finer abrasive, keeping the blend shallow and the edges faired at a ratio of 20 to 1. CAUTION: DO NOT USE A GRINDING WHEEL. LOCAL HEATING WILL CHANGE THE TEMPER OF THE SKIN. 5. Measure the remaining thickness at the deepest point and compare it with the limit. 6. Where the remaining thickness is below the limit, stop and raise a repair request. 7. Polish the blend to the finish stated in the referenced data and do a dye penetrant inspection of the blended area. WARNING: PENETRANT AND DEVELOPER ARE HARMFUL IF INHALED. USE THEM ONLY IN A VENTILATED AREA. 8. Apply the chromate-free surface protection and let it cure. 9. Apply corrosion inhibiting compound to the joint line and to the adjacent fastener heads. 10. Where the clip D5321122023477 has been disturbed, refit it with new fasteners AES645587-2A. 11. Record the blend depth and the remaining thickness on the aircraft blend map.
sections.close_out: Install the lining panels and the floor panels that were removed. Do a check of the cargo compartment drain path to confirm that it is clear. Remove the tools and the waste from the compartment. Record the blend on the aircraft structural repair record with the blend map reference and the date.

safety_precautions: Use penetrant and developer only in a ventilated area.
Do not use a grinding wheel on the skin.

tooling.description: Ultrasonic thickness gauge with 5 MHz probe

title: Blend-Out of Corrosion Damage on the Fwd Lower Shell Skin Adjacent to the Lap Joint

issue.reason: A sequencing requirement is added so that blend-out is completed before the longitudinal lap joint is re-sealed under MOD-150214.

abstract: Controlled blending of surface and intergranular corrosion from the forward lower shell skin beside the longitudinal lap joint, with the depth limits, the protection restoration, and the rule that blending is done before the joint is re-sealed.

sections.purpose: This task removes corrosion from the forward lower shell skin next to the longitudinal lap joint by controlled blending, and restores the surface protection, provided the remaining thickness stays inside the published limit. Where the aircraft is also scheduled for lap joint re-sealing under MOD-150214, this task is accomplished first, because a blend cut into a joint that has already been re-sealed destroys the new interfay bead.
sections.job_setup_note: Establish the nominal skin thickness from the structural repair data before you start, because the blend limit is a percentage of it. Ultrasonic thickness measurement is required before and after blending and the readings must be recorded on the blend map. Corrosion that reaches a fastener hole or crosses the joint line is outside the scope of this task. Read the work package before you raise the job card. If re-sealing of the longitudinal lap joint under MOD-150214 is planned in the same visit, the blend-out must be finished, measured and signed off before the joint is closed; blending after the interfay bead is laid cuts the bead and makes a second re-seal necessary.

LOCAL HEATING WILL CHANGE THE TEMPER OF THE SKIN. 5. Measure the remaining thickness at the deepest point and compare it with the limit. 6. Where the remaining thickness is below the limit, stop and raise a repair request. 7. Polish the blend to the finish stated in the referenced data and do a dye penetrant inspection of the blended area. WARNING: PENETRANT AND DEVELOPER ARE HARMFUL IF INHALED. USE THEM ONLY IN A VENTILATED AREA. 8. Apply the chromate-free surface protection and let it cure. 9. Apply corrosion inhibiting compound to the joint line and to the adjacent fastener heads. 10. type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft; to be accomplished before lap joint re-sealing under MOD-150214 where both fall in the same visit

safety_precautions: Use penetrant and developer only in a ventilated area.
Do not use a grinding wheel on the skin.
Do the blend-out before the lap joint is re-sealed when both are in the same work package.
